create.title: Direct square-root-product bilinear Poisson return
create.statement_tex: Let J=sqrt(X), T=J/Q, 1<<Q<=J^(1-delta), beta be fixed smooth compactly supported, Xi be fixed smooth compactly supported in (0,1), and C(y)=y^(3/4)Xi(2sqrt(y)). On a fixed positive ratio sector inside q>4k, T_Q=sum_(k,q odd)chi_4(q)beta(k/Q)C(k/q)e(sqrt(Xkq)) has a coefficient-preserving two-dimensional character-Poisson stationary expansion whose principal returned wavelet is W_Q=sum_(m>J)sum_(r<J odd)chi_4(r)Xi(J/m)K_beta((m/J)(X-mr)/T), with fixed ratio restrictions, and T_Q=e(1/8)Q^(3/2)J^(-1/2)W_Q+O((QJ)^(-1/2)X^epsilon). Every correction has the same Schwartz product localization. Hence T_Q<<Q^(3/2)J^(-1/2)(1+J/Q)X^epsilon. At Q=X^(1/5) this is X^(7/20+epsilon), while the target X^(3/10+epsilon) is equivalent to the still-open signed bound W_Q<<J^(1/2)X^epsilon and needs the factor J^(1/2)/Q=X^(1/20) beyond absolute counting. The two-dimensional Hessian determinant is zero, exact products and perfect-power fibres are subtarget, and the statement is fixed-smooth-interior only.
create.next_action: Prove the exact signed fixed-centre product-wavelet bound W_Q<<J^(1/2)X^epsilon without repeating Poisson, Cauchy, or completion to the full r_2 coefficient; alternatively pivot to an independent unresolved bridge obligation.

The direct two-dimensional transform is a fixed-centre product-wavelet return with the same H/L deficit. A new signed near-product theorem is required; product grouping and another Poisson transform are circular.
The direct pre-Cauchy form and two-dimensional Poisson independently return to this fixed-centre product wavelet. Only genuine signed near-product cancellation can improve the X^(7/20) direct bound.
Neither the lossless energy involution nor the weaker direct Poisson return closes the target. Do not repeat these transforms; isolate a genuinely new signed fixed-centre input.

reject.reason: The exact transform returns a length-J/Q fixed-centre product wavelet and gives only X^(7/20+epsilon) at Q=X^(1/5), missing X^(1/20).
The Hessian determinant of sqrt(Xkq) is identically zero by degree-one homogeneity; its dual aliases form the near-hyperbola mr=X+O(J/Q).
Product grouping gives Q^2 capacity, while Cauchy invokes the stronger unresolved Q^2 energy theorem. Neither proves the Q^(3/2) direct target.
The applicable published bilinear monomial bound contains an exactly trivial X^(2/5) term and therefore does not improve the direct form to X^(3/10).
The lawful singleton mapping has an X^(17/40) term, worse than trivial; the methodological analogy cannot delete it.
The best audited current exponent pair gives X^(0.388883...+epsilon), above both the X^(7/20) Poisson bound and the X^(3/10) target.
All square-product rays have only O(Q^(1+epsilon)) capacity and fourth-power fibres are smaller, below the Q^(3/2) target.
